subject: Next steps — dedicated sizing call + technical deep dive (LumenPay)
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily@lumenpay.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jun 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps — dedicated sizing call + technical deep dive (LumenPay)

Hi Emily,

Thanks again for the call earlier — great to meet you and Marco. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can lock the next step (dedicated capacity sizing + technical deep dive):

Summary of what we heard
- Primary workload: conversational text generation for customer support augmentation (mixed-turn chat, plus async batch summarization).
- Expected traffic profile: peak ~140–170 reqs/s for short-form chat bursts, steady-state ~45–70 reqs/s.
- Latency SLO: p95 <= 250ms (goal 200ms) for chat; batch jobs can be longer.
- Model: plan to start with an LLM-compatible Bloom-like open model; willing to explore quantized variants.
- Data residency: US-only for production; staging ok in multi-region.

What we propose
1) A dedicated sizing + deep-dive session where our Infra and Runtime leads walk through throughput tradeoffs, KV caching, and recommended GPU pool size.
2) Mutual Action Plan doc to capture acceptance criteria, milestones, and target launch window (attached).
3) Sample traffic file (you mentioned ops can share); having that ahead of the sizing call helps us produce a sizing matrix faster.

Possible slots (PT) — please pick whichever works for you / Marco / ops:
- Wed 6/14 10:00–11:00 or 14:00–15:00 PT
- Thu 6/15 09:00–10:00 PT
- Mon 6/19 11:00–12:00 PT

If none of those work, send 2–3 windows and well adapt.

Attachments: lumenpay-load-summary.csv (template), RWI-MAP-LumenPay.docx (mutual action plan).

Goals for the sizing call
- Confirm throughput and short/long sequence splits so we can recommend a dedicated pool (GPU type + count).
- Agree on p95 latency guardrails and fallback model variants.
- Identify a technical owner on both sides to run the spike/test (ops/dev).

Looping Nikhil (runtime lead) and Ben (AE) to ensure we have the right infra and commercial coverage.

Thanks — looking forward to locking a slot.

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ava@redwoodinference.com

Ava — thanks for the clear recap and for the MAP draft.

Quick answers from our side:
- We can share 7 days of production traffic logs (anonymized) and the per-request size histograms. Ops will export to CSV and drop it into the shared link (cc'ed).
- For the initial pilot we expect 100–150 reqs/s steady peak, but plenty of short-burst spikes during peak hours.
- p95 target 200ms is ideal; if we need to trade latency vs cost were open to options you recommend.

Availability: Wed 6/14 14:00–15:00 PT works best for Marco and me. Ops can attend if you want to walk through the logs live.

Please include any runbook or pre-read you'd like us to look at. Also loop in whoever owns billing/pricing if we need to discuss committed pool economics (happy to have that conversation after sizing).

Thanks,
Emily Zhao
Head of Platform Integrations, LumenPay
emily@lumenpay.com
